elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(b) is permissive only: "The Servicer or the Marketing Agent, as applicable, may participate in and assume the defense and settlement of a Proceeding at its expense." Section 6.3(a) merely reimburses amounts "incurred by such parties in defending themselves". No mandatory "will defend" obligation, and the Indemnified Person definition reaches only the Issuer, Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee and their officers, directors, employees and agents — not affiliates. Defect to repair: insert "will defend" and extend the Indemnified Person list to the Issuer's Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(a)(i)-(ii) indemnifies "the Issuer, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee ... and their officers, directors, employees and agents" for "claims, actions, suits, damages and liabilities". Third-party claim cover in Customer's favour exists, but the affiliate limb of the element is absent — no Affiliates of the Issuer are Indemnified Persons. Defect: add "and its Affiliates" to the Indemnified Person definition in Section 6.3(a)(i).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(a) is limited to losses "resulting from the Servicer's ... willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under the Transaction Documents". No infringement or misappropriation limb appears anywhere in the rendered language, and none was inserted. Defect: no operative IP-infringement indemnity limb exists (subject matter fit is a commercial question, but the element is textually unmet).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: The trigger in Section 6.3(a)(i) and (ii) is exhaustively "willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence"; there is no breach-of-Law trigger. Defect: add a limb for the Servicer's/Marketing Agent's violation of applicable Law.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No unauthorised-access or disclosure trigger appears, notwithstanding that Cellco acts as Custodian of the Receivable Files. Defect: add a limb covering unauthorised access to or disclosure of Obligor/Receivable File data caused by the Servicer or Custodian.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(a)(i): losses "resulting from the Servicer's (including in its capacity as Custodian) willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under the Transaction Documents"; Section 6.3(a)(ii) mirrors this for the Marketing Agent.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(b): the Indemnified Person will "promptly notify the Servicer or the Marketing Agent, as applicable, of the Proceeding", with a favourable no-forfeiture proviso absent prejudice.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(b) allocates control: the Servicer/Marketing Agent "may participate in and assume the defense and settlement of a Proceeding at its expense", must use "counsel reasonably satisfactory to the Indemnified Person", and pays separate counsel where there is a conflict.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(b) imposes only a notice obligation on the Indemnified Person; there is no cooperation covenant. The omission is Customer-favourable, but the element is textually unmet — no "reasonable cooperation" language exists.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Conditional element whose condition does not arise: the rendered operative language contains no Issuer or Depositor indemnity running to Cellco (Section 9.2 is a narrow defence-of-title covenant by the Depositor in the Issuer's favour, not an indemnity). With no Customer indemnity at all, nothing exceeds the permitted narrow scope.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3 covers only wilful misconduct, bad faith and gross negligence; there is no allegation-of-infringement or misappropriation trigger. The deterministic check "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present" returns false, consistent with the text. Defect: no IP-infringement indemnity limb drafted.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: exclusions are allowed, not required. No IP indemnity exists, so no impermissibly broad exclusion has been accepted; nothing to repair on this element.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; the condition does not arise because no IP indemnity or exclusion set has been drafted, so no Customer-adverse exclusion is present.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no exclusions appear in Section 6.3 and none has been added, so nothing exceeds the permitted carve-outs.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No mitigation remedy of any kind appears; Section 6.3 addresses only monetary indemnification and defence of Proceedings. Defect: no procure/modify/replace obligation in operative language.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund mechanic exists in Section 6.3 or elsewhere in the rendered text; the Servicer's compensation arrangements are untouched. Defect: no fallback refund obligation.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3(a) indemnifies "for all fees, expenses, losses, claims, actions, suits, damages and liabilities" with no cap at all, which exceeds (is more favourable than) a 3x annual fees super-cap; imposing the cap would newly limit an uncapped indemnity running in our favour.

reasons: Neither level is position-complete. Preferred fails on five elements: no express duty to defend (Section 6.3(b) says the Servicer "may participate in and assume the defense" — permissive), no affiliate coverage in the Indemnified Person definition, no IP-infringement limb, no breach-of-Law limb, no data-breach limb, and no cooperation covenant.

Fallback fails on the three load-bearing elements: there is no IP-infringement indemnity trigger, no procure/modify/replace mitigation obligation, and no refund-of-fees backstop. The deterministic check confirming absence of an IP indemnity matches the text in substance, not merely mechanically.

The 3x super-cap element is treated as met because Section 6.3 is presently uncapped, which is strictly better for us; the drafter is correct not to import a cap that would newly limit an uncapped indemnity.

The Customer-indemnity element is met vacuously — no Issuer or Depositor indemnity runs to Cellco in the rendered language (Section 9.2 is a narrow defence-of-title covenant), so there is nothing to narrow and drafting one would be self-harming.
Minimality and intent are preserved because no operative text was changed at all; the submission is an escalation, not a redline. That also means nothing has been repaired.

To move to a complete preferred level, the drafter must (i) change "may participate in and assume the defense" to a mandatory "will defend", (ii) add "and its Affiliates" to the Section 6.3(a)(i) Indemnified Person definition, (iii) add express limbs for violation of applicable Law and for unauthorised access to or disclosure of Obligor/Receivable File data caused by the Servicer or Custodian, and (iv) add a reasonable-cooperation sentence to Section 6.3(b).

If the business confirms the transaction has no services, deliverables, software or IP-licence subject matter, the IP-infringement/procure-modify-replace-refund construct is inapposite and should be recorded as a scoped-out element rather than left silently unaddressed; the finding should state that conclusion in the operative record, not merely in the rationale.
